description.en-US: The instruction this attempt was made for. One instruction accumulates several attempts - a failure, a correction, a retry - and reading them in order is how anyone reconstructs why a document exists or does not.

Which try this was, counting from one. Stored rather than derived from created_at because attempts are what a duplicate-issuance investigation counts, and two rows written in the same millisecond must still be orderable.

How this attempt ended. 'unknown' IS NOT A FAILURE and is the reason this resource exists: the request reached the provider and the reply did not come back, so nobody can say whether a document was created. It must be reconciled against the provider before any retry - retrying an unknown is how one sale acquires two legal invoices.
When the attempt began. Immutable: an audit record that can be back-dated is not evidence.
When the attempt finished. Null while it is still processing, and also on an attempt that ended 'unknown' before this could be written - which is itself a signal worth reading.

The idempotency key sent to the provider for this attempt. IT IS WHAT MAKES AN UNKNOWN RESOLVABLE: reconciliation asks the provider what became of this key, and without it a lost reply could never be turned into an answer.

The document reference the provider returned, on a successful attempt. Copied onto the instruction as well, so the instruction answers 'which document' without a join, while this keeps which attempt produced it.
The provider's code for this attempt's failure.
This attempt's failure in the provider's words.
